heuristic.applicability: Prefer for a still-grasped but off-timing intermediate state produced by a neighboring skill, when the current measured TCP pose is reliable and scene displacement is modest. It is designed for receding-horizon local correction across lift, turn, transport, alignment, and descent without relying on a memorized absolute phase clock.

handoff.entry_conditions: Use after closed-grasp retrieval or at an intermediate shared state when the two causal frames provide TCP/peg motion direction and peg-to-hole geometry. The policy does not require the nominal index-1120 phase, but its training support contains only successful-path intermediate states.
handoff.exit_conditions: Terminate or hand off when observed peg/hole relations show near-axis alignment and y/z centering with descent to the insertion height, using the shared [1380,1500) region for a multi-chunk transition.
handoff.failure_signatures: Local chunks oscillate or fail to reduce geometric error, TCP-relative targets accumulate drift, peg/TCP coupling is lost, clearance decreases near the box, a large scene displacement requires a globally different route, or IK is unconverged/at limits. Successful demonstrations do not establish recovery from these errors.
handoff.overlap_role: Supervise every action in [1120,1500), preserving 7.5 s incoming and 6.0 s outgoing overlap. Replanning after each 8 executed actions reanchors local displacements while the framework retains the two-frame history across switches.
handoff.successor_readiness: The insertion successor is ready when the peg is held, aligned, centered and at/descending toward hole height. If intermediate state is sound but the hole itself moved, prefer the destination-frame prior before or during outgoing overlap.

heuristic.limitations: TCP-relative chunks are locally well conditioned but not globally translation invariant to a moved destination; long-range corrections still depend on observed relative geometry learned from narrow successful demonstrations. Reanchoring cannot repair a lost grasp, dropped peg, collision, or unreachable state. A fixed anchor within each chunk may accumulate execution/model error. Use the hole-frame policy for fixture displacement and the peg-frame policy for a reliably held but displaced source.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Use as the phase/handoff-robust alternative when causal motion and geometry are reliable but nominal progress is not. Recompute the TCP anchor after every 8 executed slots, never advance state during denoising, keep slots 1-8 only, preserve incoming/outgoing action overlap, and monitor peg coupling and IK residuals before continuing.
heuristic.rationale: The demonstrations traverse qualitatively different phases inside one long slice: low lift at 1120, clearance/high lift around 1220-1270, simultaneous transport and turning around 1270-1380, and aligned descent/early insertion around 1380-1500. Timing differs: demo12205 still has peg y about 0.160 at 1380, whereas demo12208 is nearly centered at y 0.180 and begins descent earlier; end x also ranges about -0.252 to -0.185. A policy keyed mainly to absolute trajectories can issue the wrong phase after a neighboring policy hands off at a different successful intermediate state. Diffusing chunk-start-TCP-relative translation and rotation-vector targets, while conditioning on two-frame relative geometry, geometric clearance/alignment/progress cues, qpos and qvel, emphasizes the correction from the actual causal state. Reanchoring each execution chunk limits accumulated frame error. Expected robustness is to valid off-timing states represented by demonstrations, not unseen-error recovery.
heuristic.statement: Receding local-twist prior: diffuse each commanded TCP target as a chunk-start TCP-frame translation and exponential-coordinate rotation plus gripper, conditioned on two-frame robot/object state and explicit geometric phase cues. Reanchor at each 8-action replan to target handoff timing and intermediate-state ambiguity.

assignment.subgoal: Maintain the peg grasp while lifting to clearance, turning the peg into the square-hole axis, transporting it above the target, and staging it through descent and the first part of insertion.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: Encode/decode demonstration targets through the chunk TCP frame and exponential coordinates; decoded IK FK must match commanded TCP position/rotation and unchanged gripper within maximum error 0.005. Nonunique IK is permitted and explicit solver diagnostics are returned.

contract.cut_relation: Preserves every action in each assigned [1120,1500) segment, including incoming [1120,1270) and outgoing [1380,1500) overlap. Reanchoring occurs only at the framework's replan boundary; temporal slots and masks are unchanged.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is an unnormalized Cartesian target [translation(3 metres), rotation vector(3 radians), gripper(1)] for T_chunk_start_tcp^-1*T_command. The chunk anchor is the newest causal tcp_pose and is fixed during the sampled chunk. Slots are t-1 through t+14 and execution uses slots 1-8. Decoding applies the SO(3) exponential map, composes with the anchor, and calls panda_kinematics.solve_ik from freshly measured qpos. Gripper is passed through unchanged.
contract.parameter_semantics: No high-level numeric parameters. The caller passes an empty object and selects this policy for a valid but off-timing intermediate state. At every replan, the newest measured tcp_pose is the chunk action anchor.
